Left: Jump2d
Right: Leap

The most important reason why I still use leap: Its promise that the second character of the spot I am targeting can always be typed after initiating the search. That way, I have more time to process the generated third char, which is shown immediately.

I would like to use jump2d, and have been thinking about an idiomatic implementation starting from MiniJump2d.builtin.single_character:

- on start, dim immediately. Otherwise, there is no indication of activity until the user enters the first character
- n_steps_ahead should be high
- the labels should stay in place when typing
- on start, group by the second character of each spot. Generate labels as usual per group

~~I am using this [branch](https://github.com/abeldekat/mini.nvim/tree/jump2d_include_second_character) in my fork of mini.nvim.~~

Init.lua:

```lua
---@diagnostic disable: undefined-global
local function setup_deps(path_to_site)
  local mini_path = path_to_site .. "pack/deps/start/mini.nvim"
  if not vim.uv.fs_stat(mini_path) then
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    -- vim.fn.system({ "git", "clone", "--filter=blob:none", "https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim", mini_path })
    vim.fn.system({
      "git",
      "clone",
      "--filter=blob:none",
      "https://github.com/abeldekat/mini.nvim",
      "--branch=jump2d_include_second_character",
      mini_path,
    })
    vim.cmd("packadd mini.nvim | helptags ALL")
    vim.cmd('echo "Installed `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
  end
  require("mini.deps").setup({ path = { package = path_to_site } })
end
setup_deps(vim.fn.stdpath("data") .. "/site/")

local H = {}
vim.g.mapleader = " "
local setup = function()
  MiniDeps.now(function()
    require("mini.basics").setup()
    vim.cmd.colorscheme("randomhue")
    vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("FileType", {
      pattern = { "lua" },
      callback = function() pcall(vim.treesitter.start) end,
    })

    local allowed_windows = { current = true, not_current = true }
    local group_dim, ns_id_dim = "LeapBackdrop", vim.api.nvim_create_namespace("MiniJump2dDimImmediately")
    require("mini.jump2d").setup({
      allowed_windows = allowed_windows,
      hl_group = group_dim,
      hl_group_ahead = "LeapLabel",
      labels = "jkl;mhniosde",
      mappings = { start_jumping = "" },
      silent = true,
      view = { dim = false, fixed_steps = true }, -- NOTE: New property fixed_steps
    })

    local single_character_extended = function()
      H.dim_immediately(ns_id_dim, group_dim, allowed_windows)
      MiniJump2d.start(MiniJump2d.builtin_opts.single_character_extended) -- NOTE: New builtin
      H.dim_remove(ns_id_dim, allowed_windows)
    end
    vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x", "o" }, "s", single_character_extended, { desc = "Start 2d jumping" })
  end)
end

H.dim_immediately = function(ns, group, allowed_windows)
  for _, win_id in ipairs(H.list_wins(allowed_windows)) do
    local wininfo = vim.fn.getwininfo(win_id)[1]
    --stylua: ignore
    vim.highlight.range(
      wininfo.bufnr, ns, group,
      { wininfo.topline - 1, 0 }, { wininfo.botline - 1, -1 }, { priority = 9999 }
    )
  end
  vim.cmd("redraw")
end

H.dim_remove = function(ns, allowed_windows)
  for _, win_id in ipairs(H.list_wins(allowed_windows)) do
    pcall(vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace, vim.api.nvim_win_get_buf(win_id), ns, 0, -1)
  end
end

H.list_wins = function(allowed_windows)
  local win_id_init = vim.api.nvim_get_current_win()
  return vim.tbl_filter(function(win_id)
    if win_id == win_id_init then return allowed_windows.current end
    return allowed_windows.not_current
  end, vim.api.nvim_list_wins())
end

setup()
```

Notes:
- I could not find an easy way to add "dim immediately" to jump2d.lua
- I can imagine that `spots_add_steps` does not *have* to be public. Perhaps an internal table, returning a custom function when the spotter has a certain id?

cc: @pkazmier 

See also: [Improve 'mini.jump2d' default config and jumping experience](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/issues/1818)

comment_data.body:
Thanks for sharing!

> * on start, dim immediately. Otherwise, there is no indication of activity until the user enters the first character

This for me breaks the purpose of dimming in the first place: indicate that certain lines have matches (while making labels more visible). If there is dimming before jumping has started, then this interpretation breaks (as before jumping all lines are dimmed). I don't think I like that.

> * n_steps_ahead should be high
> * the labels should stay in place when typing

Unfortunately, both of these do not go well together, because labels can overlap. Like in case of several consecutive same characters for `single_character` case. If they stay in place, not-first character of label sequence can be hidden behind the labels from the right neighbor match.

There are solutions, of course. Like dynamically hiding already typed letter of matched spots (to clear the space for possible later labels from left to be visible). Or like showing only a single step ahead (like 'leap.nvim' seems to be doing).

But I am not a fan of showing labels not at the target spot. Every time I tried it, it was always confusing to adapt to.

In theory, showing labels one or two steps to the right is possible with a tweaked spotter:
- Actually match spots that are one or two steps to the right of the target ones.
- Use `hooks.after_jump` to adjust cursor.

This would still only show labels after one or two keys are typed, yes.

> I would say that the main hurdle is the guarantee that for each spot the first two labels equal the first two characters. Thus, for each spot, user knows the first two labels beforehand. In order to take advantage of that knowledge, it is necessary to show spot's second character and generated label directly after typing its first character.

Showing second character and generated label(s) is not tied to user knowing the "first two labels beforehand". There is a mix of terminology here:
- Jump spots are visible cells that user might want to jump to. They are computed with spotter, which is the first step of jumping.
- Labels are what is computed and visualized to filter one out of many possible jump spots. Generated labels use *only* characters from `config.labels`.

This allows several workflows after jumping is started:
- All jump spots are precomputed by some algorithm (default, word start, etc.), their generated labels are shown, user needs to filter them out. This is the initial and current primary design of 'mini.jump2d'.
- User is required to press single key (which will be a "jumper identifier") to decide how target spots are computed. After that spots are computed, labels are shown, user filters through them. This is how `builtin_opts.single_character` works and what is planned as the new design of #1818.

The second approach can be extended to also fit the "type *two* characters to compute spots":
- User presses jumper identifier, let's say `p`. Its spotter is configured in such a way that it requires pressing *another* character before computing jump spots. So it waits for the user key press, let's say `a`.
- Spotter then computes all jump spots that match `pa`.
- If there are several, labels are shown and user filters them until there is one left. By default labels are shown at the place the jump will happen (i.e. starting over `p` and to the right of `a`), but it should be possible to show them just to the right of `a` via tweaking how spotter computes jump spots and later adjusting cursor in `hooks.after_jump`.

Hope this makes sense.

Using my local [fork](https://github.com/abeldekat/mini.nvim/tree/jump2d_extended_character), I added some improvements, especially for buffers without much text. 

Quite often, when supplying `jump initializer -> second character`, there is no generated label because the combination is unique. I now show the [middledot](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/bb0368efa95acb55063ead78b5c93e54648900cd/lua/akmini/jump2d_leaped.lua#L927) on target position in that case.

Sometimes, the jump is immediate when the `jump initializer` is unique. For example, in the video below, in the last jump to `workflow/visits.lua`, the `v` is unique. 
When I type the first two characters, the second `i` enters insert mode... I added an extra [option](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/bb0368efa95acb55063ead78b5c93e54648900cd/lua/ak/workflow/jump2d.lua#L65) to [MiniJump2d.start](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/bb0368efa95acb55063ead78b5c93e54648900cd/lua/akmini/jump2d_leaped.lua#L345) to prevent that, forcing the second character to always be requested:

```lua
---...

  if #spots == 1 and not opts.force_filtering then
    H.perform_jump(spots[1], opts.hooks.after_jump)
    return
  end

---...
```

These changes are especially nice in `mini.files`, in combination with file `after/ftplugin/minifiles.lua`:

```lua
vim.b.minijump2d_config = {
  allowed_windows = { current = true, not_current = false },
}
```

By default, inside mini.files labels are also generated in all other windows, which is not necessary.


I am also experimenting with the labels, trying to increase the chance of being able to alternate between the left and right hand:

``` lua
  -- Have left hand labels grouped around s:
  labels = "jskdlwmeixoc", -- 12 labels alternated "js", "kd", "lw", "me", "ix", "oc"
```
